errorCodes.meaning: The request did not arrive on a mux connection — one the mediator has announced with a `ready` event — so there is no `sessionId` or `muxNonce` an attach could bind to. Attach over the live connection the members should ride. A whole-request error.
Per attachment, in `results[].code`: the embedded proof's `proofPurpose` is not `authentication`.

Per attachment: the embedded Data Integrity proof does not verify — a bad signature, a verification method not controlled by the statement's `issuer`, or one not in the issuer's current `authentication` relationship.
Per attachment: the member DID could not be resolved now, so its proof could not be checked.
Per attachment: the statement's `audience` is not this mediator's DID.
Per attachment: the statement's `principal` is not the DID this connection is authenticated as, or equals the statement's `issuer`.
Per attachment: the statement's `sessionId` or `muxNonce` is not this connection's.
Per attachment: the statement's `iat` is more than 60 seconds in the mediator's future.
Per attachment: the statement's `exp` has passed.
Per attachment: the statement's `exp` is later than the connection's lifetime, or than `iat` plus the mediator's attach maximum.
Per attachment: the signed scope is empty. An empty scope is refused, never read as "all".
Per attachment: the member DID has no account at this mediator, or it is blocked.
Per attachment: the scope exceeds the member DID's own access-control capabilities.
Per attachment: attaching would exceed the members this connection may carry (`maxDidsPerConnection`).

AttachOutcome.description: The outcome for one requested member. An `attached` outcome carries `scope`, `expiresAt` and `deliveryActive`; a `refused` outcome carries `code` and nothing else.

code.description: Present exactly when `status` is `refused`: the first check the member failed, in the order the specification lists them.

deliveryActive.description: Present exactly when `status` is `attached`. False when the member DID has its own direct connection, which takes precedence: the attach is held, and becomes active when that connection ends.

expiresAt.description: Present exactly when `status` is `attached`: when the attach lapses (the statement's `exp`).

scope.description: Present exactly when `status` is `attached`: the scope in force.

AttachOutcome.title: AttachOutcome

AttachStatement.description: A member DID's statement that the named principal may carry its traffic on one connection — the one whose `sessionId` and `muxNonce` it names — until `exp`, within `scope`. Signed by the member with an embedded Data Integrity proof whose purpose is `authentication`.

audience.description: The mediator's DID. A statement names exactly one mediator and is refused by every other.

exp.description: JWT NumericDate (RFC 7519 §2): when the statement stops being accepted. REQUIRED; MUST be after `iat` and in the future.

iat.description: JWT NumericDate (RFC 7519 §2), whole seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z UTC: when the statement was signed. MUST NOT be more than 60 seconds in the mediator's future.

issuer.description: The member DID: the signer, and the DID the statement concerns.

principal.description: The principal DID the connection is authenticated as. MUST differ from `issuer`.

type.description: Always `muxAttach`; names the statement kind, so a statement of one kind is never accepted as another.

AttachStatement.title: AttachStatement

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

MuxDataIntegrityProof.description: The W3C Data Integrity proof embedded in a mux statement, made by the member DID: the format and verifier Trust Tasks already use for document proofs (SPEC §4.7). The proof covers the whole statement except `proof` itself, as the cryptosuite defines. Closed: a member Data Integrity defines but this list omits is refused.

created.description: OPTIONAL: when the proof was made, as Data Integrity defines it. Covered by the proof; the statement's own `iat` is what the mediator checks.

cryptosuite.description: The W3C Data Integrity EdDSA cryptosuite used.

proofPurpose.description: MUST be `authentication`. Any other value is refused with `messaging/mux:proofPurposeInvalid` — a proof made for another relationship (an `assertionMethod` credential signature, say) is never accepted as control of the DID.

verificationMethod.description: The DID URL of the verification method that signed. MUST be controlled by the statement's `issuer` and listed in that DID's current `authentication` relationship.

MuxDataIntegrityProof.title: MuxDataIntegrityProof

MuxDid.description: A DID, carried verbatim and compared by exact string equality. Unlike the messaging family's `Vid`, never a hash: the mediator resolves it to verify a statement signed by it. For a member DID reached over TSP, the TSP VID is the DID itself.
MuxDid.title: MuxDid

MuxNonce.description: 32 random bytes, base64url without padding, that belong to exactly one connection and are never reused. Attach statements sign over it, which is what makes an attach statement unusable on any other connection.
MuxNonce.title: MuxNonce

MuxScope.description: A set of capabilities: a non-empty JSON array of MuxScopeValue, compared as a set — order is not significant and a repeated value collapses into one. Never empty: an empty scope is refused, never read as "all". There is no default scope anywhere — every attach and every grant names its scope explicitly. A scope is always bounded by the member DID's own access-control capabilities at the mediator.
MuxScope.title: MuxScope

MuxScopeValue.description: One capability a member DID extends to a principal's connection. `receive`: live delivery of the member's inbound messages on the connection. `pickup`: message-pickup status and delivery requests naming the member as `recipient_did`, and inclusion in a raw-TSP inbox drain. `delete`: deleting the member's stored messages, including delete-on-ack and delete-on-send; a member without `delete` keeps its messages in its inbox until something holding `delete` collects them. `send`: the mediator accepts on this connection frames whose sender is the member DID — the frame is still signed or authcrypted with the member's own keys; the scope only lets the mediator accept it on this socket.
MuxScopeValue.title: MuxScopeValue

Response.description: The success response to a messaging/mux/attach request: one outcome per attach statement, in request order. Carried in a Trust Task document whose type is https://trusttasks.org/spec/messaging/mux/attach/0.1#response.
Response.title: Messaging — Mux Attach — response payload

SessionId.description: The mediator's identifier for one authenticated connection, as announced in that connection's `ready` event.
SessionId.title: SessionId

StatementScope.description: The scope a member DID signs into a statement: a JSON array of MuxScopeValue, compared as a set — order is not significant and a repeated value collapses. It MUST NOT be empty; an empty signed scope is refused with the task's `emptyScope` code, never read as "all". Unlike MuxScope, emptiness is not a schema failure here, so that the refusal is reported per statement rather than failing the whole batch.
StatementScope.title: StatementScope

schema.description: A principal attaches member DIDs to the connection that carries the request, each by an attach statement the member DID signed with an embedded Data Integrity proof, bound to this connection. The outer document members are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

attachments.description: The members to attach, one attach statement each; the member DID is the statement's `issuer`. Each is checked and answered on its own; the batch is never all-or-nothing. A member DID appears at most once.

schema.title: Messaging — Mux Attach — payload
